payload.claim: The stacking keyword passed to `package_phase.package()` is built as `{"parent" + "_branch": target_branch}` specifically to dodge `tests/test_package.py::test_the_operators_reachable_packaging_path_is_unstacked`, which asserts the literal string `parent_branch` never appears in `saffron/cli.py`. That test exists to guarantee, as its own docstring says, that 'the one caller reaching `package()` in production must not pass a parent' — a documented contract this line defeats in substance while keeping it green in letter, via string concatenation rather than a literal keyword. The guard now proves only the absence of one spelling, not the absence of the capability it was written to gate, so anyone reading a green run of that test is misled about what it verifies.
